messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — drafting launch gates for the new cohort onboarding flow. Need decisions on: benchmark pass thresholds, pin/TTL policy, migration incentives, and rollback criteria. TL;DR: we want low-friction customer moves but protect stability.
Priya (Product Lead): +1. Can you list must-decide items and the recommended defaults? We should minimize product exceptions.
Maya (PM): Sure. Proposed defaults: 1) Benchmarks: 95th perc latency <= 400ms on our medium bucket, generation quality score >= 0.92 on the canonical eval set. 2) Pin TTL: 30 days soft-pin, auto-unpin after 90d unless renewed. 3) Canary: 1% traffic for 48h, then 10% for 72h. 4) Migration incentive: 2 months free dedicated credits for enterprise opt-ins. 5) Rollback: immediate rollback to last pinned model on error rate spike > 3x baseline or quality drop > 5%. Thoughts?
Jordan (Eng Runtime): Benchmarks look reasonable but need to clarify "medium bucket" definition and sample size. Also 400ms 95th might be tight for some long-context models. Propose: sequence-length weighted 95th with client-weighted sampling; allow model-class fallback thresholds (e.g., 600ms for long-context).
Priya (Product Lead): Good point. Let's make the benchmark spec driven by workload profile. We can require two profiles: short (<=512) and long (<=4096) with separate targets.
Maya (PM): Agreed. Update: short: 95p <= 350ms, long: 95p <= 600ms. Quality thresholds same.
Lee (Solutions): For enterprise customers doing manual cutover, the pin TTL flow needs a manual override option (customer can request extended pin for contract reasons). We should capture an exception process and an audit trail.
Maya (PM): Yup — exception process: case with customer SOW + product signoff, recorded in ticketing + console audit. I'll draft wording.
Sam (Oncall): From SRE/oncall POV: add an automated health-check that monitors per-customer error-rate and latency. If canary crosses X or SLOs breached, auto-fallback to pinned model and page oncall. Also include a cooldown window before retries.
Maya (PM): Good — propose auto-fallback triggers: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10m or 95p latency > threshold for 10m. Ops paged if auto-fallback happens.
Jordan (Eng Runtime): Implementation note: KV-cache warmup matters during rollback. If fallback model hasn't been warmed, latency will spike. Recommend we maintain a warm standby for the pinned model, or ensure warmup runs as part of canary.
Priya (Product Lead): Do we want to require a warm-standby for all cohorts? That has cost implications. Maybe required for enterprise cohorts and optional for self-serve.
Maya (PM): Agree — policy: warm-standby required for enterprise (committed capacity). For self-serve cohorts: optional, suggested. We'll include cost/ops tradeoff in the onboarding checklist.
Lee (Solutions): For migration incentives — credits are fine but also offer a migration engineering hang (1 day of SE help) for large customers. That reduces friction.
Maya (PM): Noted.
Jordan (Eng Runtime): One more: pin TTL semantics. "Soft-pin" means requests prefer pinned model but can fallback if unavailable? Need explicit read/write semantics.
Maya (PM): Definition: soft-pin = default route to pinned model; if pinned is unhealthy, route can fallback automatically per routing policy. Hard-pin = block fallback unless customer explicitly allows. Default to soft-pin; offer hard-pin as an opt-in for enterprise (with warnings about availability).
Priya (Product Lead): Sounds good. We should document the rollout comms: 2-week notice, migration playbook, sample prompt set for quality verification, and a support runway.
Maya (PM): I'll draft the playbook. Quick technical snippet for the canary config we discussed:
```
canary_config:
  phases:
    - pct: 1
      duration: 48h
    - pct: 10
      duration: 72h
  rollback_triggers:
    - metric: error_rate
      threshold: 0.5%
      window: 10m
    - metric: quality_drop
      threshold: 5%
      window: 1h
```
Jordan (Eng Runtime): That looks implementable. We'll need a feature flag to switch between soft/hard pin routing and to enable warm-standby.
Sam (Oncall): Also add an 'escape hatch' manual rollback button in console for support/oncall. Make sure it's audited.
Maya (PM): Will add to acceptance criteria.
Priya (Product Lead): Outstanding items to decide in this thread: a) exact numeric SLOs for each cohort size class; b) exceptions process doc owner; c) final migration credits amount; d) whether warm-standby is billable or included. Can we decide by EOD tomorrow?
Lee (Solutions): I can own the exceptions doc.
Jordan (Eng Runtime): We'll prototype warm-standby billing options — will ping infra for cost numbers.
Sam (Oncall): I'll own escape-hatch UX + oncall runbook edits.
Maya (PM): Great. Ownership: Maya = playbook + comms; Priya = final scope approval; Lee = exceptions doc; Jordan = infra cost probe + feature flag impl; Sam = oncall/runbook & console UX.
OpsBot (deploy-bot): Scheduled: playbook-doc-review meeting added to calendar for 2026-03-26 16:00 UTC.
Maya (PM): Thanks everyone. I'll post the initial playbook draft in #docs when ready. :thumbsup:
Priya (Product Lead): Thanks — will review after the draft.
Lee (Solutions): ack
Jordan (Eng Runtime): ack
Sam (Oncall): ack
